name: SAR Televenture Ltd
tagline: A working-capital-heavy telecom-tower and optical-fibre EPC play riding the BSNL 4G/5G build - but ~6% ROCE / ~9.5% ROE fails the quality gate outright.
business_overview: Telecom infrastructure provider: installs and maintains small/low-cost 4G/5G cell towers (Rs 2-3 lakh/tower) and lays optical fibre cable, then leases towers back to operators (Airtel, BSNL, Jio, Vodafone). Order pipeline is heavily BSNL-linked (rural / Tier-3 4G rollout). Seeded as an external lead from X triage (@BeatTheStreet10, untrusted) citing consistent tower scaling and the OFC-laying foray.
fundamentals_table: roughly Rs 264 - Rs 106 (post-split figures vary by source)
BSNL Rs 82,900 Cr infusion; 4G/5G rural rollout
fundamentals_narrative: SAR Televenture sits in front of a genuine demand event - the BSNL 4G/5G rural build and broader tower/OFC capex - and keeps a clean, near-debt-free balance sheet. But the returns are poor: ~6% ROCE and ~9.5% ROE over three years, with working-capital days ballooning from 95 to 159 and debtor days from 86 to 115. That is the signature of a low-margin EPC contractor exposed to government-payment cycles, not a compounding infrastructure owner. The BSNL capex bulge is also a one-time program, not a structural annuity.
technical_read: Small-cap, wide post-listing/post-split range; not pulled - the verdict turns on return ratios, not the chart.
sentiment_summary: ValuePickr thread 158987 exists but is dead - 2 posts, one substantive (Aug-2024, @anupammahor, not a trusted user) laying out the bull case (400 cell sites then, >Rs 2,000 Cr BSNL pipeline). No activity since. Assessment is web/filings-based.
community_signal: No trusted-user activity. One stale 2024 bull writeup from a non-trusted user. External lead: @BeatTheStreet10 (untrusted X triage).
bse_notes: No SEBI / fraud action found. The monitorable is working-capital quality - rising debtor and WC days against a government-heavy (BSNL) order book.
bull_case: BSNL 4G/5G rural rollout + Rs 82,900 Cr government infusion is a real near-term demand driver
Tower lease-back model can build a recurring rental base over time
Blue-chip operator client list (Airtel, BSNL, Jio, Vi)
bear_case: ~6% ROCE / ~9.5% ROE - fails the screen's quality gate on its own
Working-capital days 95 -> 159, debtor days 86 -> 115 - deteriorating cash cycle
Low-margin EPC economics with heavy government-payment dependence
BSNL capex is a one-time program, not a structural annuity
Dead ValuePickr thread; single live source is an untrusted X account
verdict_headline: Real demand event but contractor-grade economics - ~6% ROCE, deteriorating working capital. thesis_fit 'neither' (hard), conviction Low.
verdict_reasoning: four_box: tailwind weak (BSNL 4G/5G build is real but lumpy, government-dependent and a one-time program), tam weak (tower + OFC EPC is competitive and low-margin), moat no (EPC contractor, no pricing power, working-capital heavy), valuation no (~6% ROCE / ~9.5% ROE does not support Rs 448 Cr; fails quality gate) -> score 1.0
Conviction Low: fails the ROCE/ROE quality gate; rising working-capital intensity; no trusted signal
No value_chain block (thin optical/telecom-infra exposure, not genuine AI-cluster optics; no deep read)
No red-flag tier (solvent, near-debt-free, no SEBI action)

four_box.note: moat = no and valuation = no (EPC contractor economics, ~6% ROCE / ~9.5% ROE, deteriorating working capital). tailwind/tam weak (lumpy government-driven tower+OFC EPC). Score <=1.5 -> thesis_fit 'neither', hard.
